(03/03/2016) Per S.K. Gangele J The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. for quashment of the criminal proceedings registered against the petitioners on a complaint vide complaint case No. 246/1998 under Section 2, 7(1), 16(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

2. On 18/08/1994, Food Inspector along with his team inspected the workshop of the petitioners Chandrakala Sweets at Jabalpur, it was noticed that Sweet and Namkeen was being prepared in the workshop, the Food Inspector had taken sample of the Sunflower Oil of Sundrop Brand which was used in the preparation of the sweet and Namkeen.

It is said that he opened the seal pack of 10 Kg.
Tin of Sunflower Oil of Sundrop Brand and took the sample of 375 gms. of Oil the sample was M.Cr.C. No. 2747/2014.
sealed, it was sent for analysis to the State Food Laboratory, Bhopal vide memorandum dated 19/08/1994.

The Public Analysis vide report dated 16/09/1994 found the sample adulterated,
thereafter, a case against the petitioners was filed after taking permission from the Dy. Director Food and Drugs Administration Jabalpur.
3.
The petitioners pleaded that the complaint was filed on 01/04/1998 after a period of four years.
The petitioners were deprived from their valuable right granted under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to get sample examined by a Central Food Laboratory.

It is further pleaded by the petitioners that the sample was taken from 10Kg. seal pack Tin Super refined Sunflower Oil, Sundrop Brand and the petitioners were not responsible for the alleged adulteration.

sentences.text: Sikandrawad were also made accused, they filed a petition before this Court and this Court vide order dated 04/03/2004 quashed the proceedings.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that petitioners have been deprived from their valuable right granted under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

Hence,
the proceedings are liable to be quashed.

In support of his contention learned counsel relied on the judgment of this Court delivered in M.Cr.C. No. 1434/1999 M.Cr.C. No. 2747/2014.
dated 04/03/2004.
5. The proceedings were initiated against the petitioners in the year 1998, there is no stay in the case, hence it is not clear that what is the stage of the trial.
The petitioners further pleaded that life of the product was three years.
The Food Inspector received the report of Public Analysis on 19/08/1994.

Copy of the report was not supplied to the applicant by the Food Inspector, hence, it is violation of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, however, this finding has to be recorded by the trial court after verifying the record and taking evidence of Food Inspector to the effect that whether the report of Public Analysis was served on the petitioners within time or not and whether the sample was taken in a seal pack container or not.
6. After recording a definite findings of facts on the aforesaid issue, it can be decided that whether there is violation of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The case is pending before the Magistrate for more than 10 years.
The record of the case has been summoned and it is kept in this file.
Looking to the aforesaid facts of the case, the petitioners can very well take the aforesaid objection during the trial.
7. Hence, this petition is disposed of with the observation that the petitioner can very well take the objection taken by M.Cr.C. No. 2747/2014.
them in this petition during the trial and the trial court shall consider the same in accordance with law.
8. Office is directed to send the record to the Lower Court for trial.
9. With the aforesaid observation, the petition is disposed of.
(S.K. GANGELE) JUDGE MISHRA M.Cr.C. No. 2747/2014.
HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH PRINCIPAL SEAT AT JABALPUR M.Cr.C. No. 2747/2014.
